subject: MAP: cost preflight — unit-econ checks for CerebraLabs pilot
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@cerebralabs.com>, CerebraLabs Procurement <procurement@cerebralabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: cost preflight — unit-econ checks for CerebraLabs pilot

Hi Elena / Procurement team —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our mutual action plan kickoff, I’m sending a lightweight preflight focused on the cost & unit-economics checks we’d like to lock before the 5-day eval. Two attachments: a one-sheet MAP draft (cerebral_map_draft.xlsx) and our working token-econ assumptions (token_econ_assumptions.pdf).

Key asks for CerebraLabs to confirm / provide:
- Typical request mix: % chat/generation vs. embeddings vs. reranking (rough split ok).
- Representative prompt + response lengths (median & 90th perc).
- Expected QPS and peak bursts (e.g., 30r/s sustained, 200r/s burst for 60s).
- Any caching/PII constraints (TTL, scope of prefix caching, hashed keys vs raw).
- Success criteria for the eval (cost per 1M tokens target, latency SLOs).

Our proposed MAP checks for the eval (short version):
- Baseline tokens-per-dollar model using int8 quantized model + batching & prefix caching.
- Default assumptions (to be validated): avg tokens/op = 800, cache hit = 35%, avg batch size (peak) = 4, tokens-per-$ target = ~1.1M (post-ops).
- Acceptance gates: end-to-end P99 < 350ms for generation flows OR documented business exception, cost within +/−20% of modeled value, cache hit >= 25% during eval.

Next steps / timeline I propose:
1) By EOD Tue (8/17): CerebraLabs shares sample traffic (anonymized).
2) Redwood runs a 5-business-day eval in a Dedicated sandbox with the MAP config (batching, KV prefix caching, prefetch of top intents).
3) After eval: joint readout + decision meeting (target week of 8/24).

I’ll hold a call slot Tue 8/17 10am PT to walk through the assumptions if useful — ok to add your procurement contact to that invite.

Attachments: cerebral_map_draft.xlsx (MAP timeline, milestones), token_econ_assumptions.pdf (assumption table & sensitivity).

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0192

Subject: Re: MAP: cost preflight — unit-econ checks for CerebraLabs pilot

Jonas —

Appreciate the clear asks. Procurement and engineering are aligned on doing a short eval but we need a few clarifications before we share anonymized traffic: 

1) Request mix: our product team says ~70% chat (multi-turn customer messages), 25% single-shot classification/embedding, 5% batch rerank. Is that fine for your assumptions?
2) Caching: we can do prefix hashing for templated prompts but anything with PII must be excluded — TTL max 6 hours. Is Redwood able to scope caching rules per route?
3) Batch windows: our internal SLAs prefer < 200ms added latency. How do you define a safe batch timeout vs. throughput gain?

Procurement will share an initial SOW template and a list of compliance questions (SOC/Security) by EOD Tue. We’ll also attach a sample, anonymized traffic extract (CSV) by Tue evening.

If those timelines work I’ll accept the 8/17 slot and add our procurement lead.

—Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Product Operations, CerebraLabs
elena.torres@cerebralabs.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MAP: cost preflight — unit-econ checks for CerebraLabs pilot

Internal notes / recommended default assumptions to surface quickly for the call: (these will be validated against the sample traffic)

- Request mix accepted: 70% generation, 25% embeddings/classify, 5% rerank. We’ll model separately per route.
- Tokens per op (current working): median prompt = 320 tokens, median model response = 480 tokens => total median = 800 tokens/op. 90th = 2,100 tokens/op.
- Caching: prefix caching expected to cover templated prompts (estimated hit 30–45% depending on UI patterns). We will instrument at route-level so CerebraLabs can opt-in/out per route; PII-exclusion rules respected (no raw free-text caching). TTL default = 6h as requested.
- Batching: safe batch timeout = 10ms for 99th of requests; effective avg batch size = 3.5 at peak (we’ll use 4 for cost modeling). If CerebraLabs needs <=200ms added latency, we can increase concurrency and lower timeout, trading cost for latency.
- Model/quantization impact: int8 (or 4-bit where validated) can reduce per-token compute by ~25–40% depending on model. We’ll include a quality delta check with a manual eval set during the 5-day run.
- Tokens-per-$ baseline (modeled):
  • unoptimized: ~400k tokens / $1
  • with batching + prefix caching + int8: ~1.05M tokens / $1 (this aligns with Jonas’s rough number).

Acceptance criteria (proposed):
- Functional: correctness on eval prompt set (F1 / business metric TBD), no >2% quality regression vs. golden baseline.
- Performance: P99 end-to-end < 350ms for primary generation route OR approved SLA exception documented in MAP.
- Cost: realized tokens-per-$ within −20% / +30% of modelled value under representative traffic.

I’ll attach the working assumptions sheet to the MAP doc; we should drive Elena toward sharing the sample traffic so we can replace priors with real numbers.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP: cost preflight — unit-econ checks for CerebraLabs pilot

Elena — thanks, that all sounds good and the timelines are fine from our side. Quick summary and next concrete steps (MAP-aligned):

1) CerebraLabs to share by EOD Tue 8/17: anonymized sample traffic extract + procurement SOW (we’ll treat the data as PII-sensitive and follow exclusion rules).
2) Redwood to provision Dedicated eval environment (sandbox) and configure route-level caching rules (PII exclusion + 6h TTL) and batching profile (10ms timeout, up to 4x ideal batch).
3) 5-business-day eval to run 8/18–8/24: Redwood will run a cost sweep (no-quant, int8, int4 where safe) + batching/caching sensitivity and return a short readout deck.
4) Joint readout week of 8/24: review cost model, quality regression checks against the golden set, and a recommended production configuration.

Acceptance gates: Karthik’s suggestions above — we’ll codify them into the MAP doc and lock the signoff criteria on the readout. If procurement needs it, we can also produce a short finance appendix showing tokens-per-$ sensitivity across hit-rate / batch-size axes.

I’ll send an updated MAP with explicit gating checkboxes and a calendar invite for Wed 8/18 9am PT to review the sample traffic ingestion plan.

Thanks all — looking forward to running this.

Jonas Weber
